subject.title: Group chat context handling can blur which messages are addressed to the current agent

question: Should OpenClaw add durable per-message target attribution for multi-agent group history, and what sibling-bot identity source and target-state semantics should become the core/plugin contract?
rationale: The code gap is source-visible, but the permanent API shape affects core prompt context, Telegram plugin metadata, and future channel/plugin behavior, so automation should not choose the contract alone.

options.title: Approve Generic Target Metadata
options.body: Add optional current-bot, other-bot, and ambient target metadata to history/reply context, populate Telegram first, and document the channel/plugin contract for future channels.

options.title: Keep Prompt Mitigation Only
options.body: Treat the existing group prompt guidance and the open prompt PR as sufficient for now, leaving durable per-message metadata deferred.

options.title: Defer To External Or Channel-Specific Experiments
options.body: Keep core unchanged until a plugin or channel-specific implementation proves the exact behavior and API need with live evidence.

recommendation.title: Approve Generic Target Metadata
recommendation.body: Add optional current-bot, other-bot, and ambient target metadata to history/reply context, populate Telegram first, and document the channel/plugin contract for future channels.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is connected to the central history/group prompt path and owns the current prompt-level mitigation discussion most closely among the observed history signals.
